about: A giant's stirring from the heat it sends out (track WS, design SSE4-stirred-clouds-design.md sections 3.2 and 3.3): the power into eddies, an eddy's speed by its width, and whether the band's shear holds an eddy or tears it apart.

params.description: share of the heat flowing through the air that ends up as eddy motion. Fitted (WS2): set so Jupiter's eddies at band width at 45 degrees run at the 17 m/s its bands already use, with the cascade constant 3

Salyk, C., Ingersoll, A. P., Lorre, J., Vasavada, A. and Del Genio, A. D. 2006, Interaction between eddies and mean flow in Jupiter's atmosphere: analysis of Cassini imaging data, Icarus 185, 430: the power eddies put into Jupiter's jets (unverified). doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2006.08.007

equation.name: Power that heat puts into a giant's eddies

F.name: heat the air sends out: from inside plus absorbed sunlight

p0.name: pressure at the base of the weather layer

eta.name: share of the heat that becomes eddy motion

eps.name: power into eddies per kilogram of the weather layer

source.text: Kraichnan 1967, Phys. Fluids 10, 1417; efficiency fitted on Jupiter (Salyk et al. 2006 give eddy power of this order)
source.where: the energy rate of two-dimensional turbulence

explain.curious: Heat leaving a giant has to stir its air on the way out; the more heat, the harder its storms and eddies churn.
explain.science: The heat flux F through a layer of mass p0/g per square metre, times an efficiency, is the energy rate per unit mass fed to the eddies. The efficiency is fitted once on Jupiter; every other giant follows from its own heat and gravity.

params.description: the constant of the cube-root law, about 3 (Kraichnan's inverse cascade; unverified)

atoms.shown: u(L) = C (ε L)^(1/3), at most √(R T / M)

equation.name: How fast an eddy of a given width turns
equation.formula: u = min(Cc * cbrt(eps * L), sqrt(R * T / M))

M.name: mean molar mass of the air

explain.curious: Bigger eddies spin faster at their edges, but only as the cube root of their size: an eddy eight times wider runs twice as fast.
explain.science: In flat turbulence fed with energy at rate ε the speed at scale L goes as (ε L)^(1/3). Capped at the isothermal speed of sound, past which the air no longer moves as a thin sheet.

equation.name: Whether a band's shear holds an eddy or tears it apart
equation.formula:
x = zeta / omega
k = 2 * sqrt(2) - 3
torn = if x < k then 1 else 0
d = max(x * x + 6 * x + 1, 0)
lambda = if x < k then sqrt(2) - 1 else (1 + x + sqrt(d)) / 2
life = if x < k then 1 / abs(zeta) else 0

zeta.name: the band's own vorticity where the eddy sits, signed as the eddy's turning

lambda.name: the steady shape's length along the wind over its width

torn.name: 1 when no steady shape exists and the shear tears the eddy apart

life.name: how long a torn eddy lasts: one shear time (0 when it holds)

explain.curious: A band's winds stretch every eddy in it. An eddy turning the same way as the shear is drawn into an oval and lives; one turning against it is pulled apart within a few hours to days.
explain.science: Moore and Saffman's steady elliptical patch in a shear flow. Its aspect λ solves ζ/ω = λ(λ − 1)/(λ + 1). Below ζ/ω = 2√2 − 3 no real λ exists: the patch is torn, here in one shear time.

equation.name: How long a cloud deck takes to fall out and be made anew
equation.formula:
mu = mu3 * (T / T3) ^ mun
lam = mu / p * sqrt(pi * R * T / (2 * M))
kn = lam / r
cc = 1 + kn * (A1 + A2 * exp(-A3 / kn))
v = 2 * r * r * rho * g / (9 * mu) * cc
tau = dz / v

T.name: temperature of the air in the deck

M.name: mean molar mass of the air

tau.name: how long the deck takes to fall out and be made anew

source.where: the slip-corrected fall of a small sphere

explain.curious: Cloud is not forever: its ice crystals slowly fall out and new ones form. Small crystals in thin air drift down for weeks to months, and that is how long the winds have to stir the cloud.
explain.science: Stokes drag on a sphere, corrected for slip when the gas's mean free path is not small beside the particle (Cunningham, with Allen and Raabe's constants). The deck lasts as long as its particles take to fall through it.

equation.name: How many tall storms the heat from inside needs
equation.formula:
rp = Ld / 2
N = s * Fi * 4 * pi * a * a / (Fp * pi * rp * rp)
Fc = s * Fi

Fi.name: heat from inside, averaged over the sphere

Ld.name: the deformation radius where plumes rise

Fp.name: heat flux inside an active plume

s.name: share of the internal heat plumes carry

Fc.name: heat the plumes carry up, over the whole sphere

source.where: moist convection carrying the internal heat

explain.curious: A giant's inner heat climbs to the cloud tops in tall thunderstorms. The more heat, the more of them: Jupiter has dozens at once, Uranus hardly any.
explain.science: If each plume carries a set heat flux over a disc half a deformation radius across, the internal heat fixes how many are alive. The ratio between worlds does not depend on the plume flux.

equation.name: How fast rising and sinking air renews a cloud deck
equation.formula:
q = x * Mg / M
dm = pb * (1 - exp(-th)) / g
ru = Fc / (L * q * dm)
tau = tf / (1 + tf * ru)

Fc.name: heat the plumes carry up, over the whole sphere

L.name: latent heat of the deepest condensate

x.name: its share of the air below its cloud, by molecules

M.name: mean molar mass of the air

pb.name: pressure at the top deck's base

th.name: the deck's thickness in scale heights

tf.name: how long the deck takes to fall out

ru.name: how fast air crossing the deck replaces it

tau.name: how long the deck lasts before it is made anew

source.where: moist convection carrying the internal heat; its return flow sinks through the decks

explain.curious: Cloud is renewed two ways: its crystals fall out, and air rising through it brings new vapour while sinking air dries it out. The more heat a giant sends up from inside, the faster its clouds turn over, so Jupiter's are younger than Uranus's.
explain.science: Each kilogram of rising air carries the latent heat of the water it condenses lower down, so the heat the plumes carry fixes the air mass crossing each square metre. The deck's own air mass over that flux is its overturn time; the two losses add as rates.
